faults.fault: At 1.5x height the cabinet body texture is stretched and smeared: vertical streaks run through the screen surround and the panel below the control deck, and the marquee/screen area shows ghosted doubled artwork. The background panel is being stretched, not tiled.

At 2.0x width the deck spans the full width but the repeated middle carries no second joystick, button cluster or start button -- the right half of the deck is blank panel plus the counter decal. A wider cabinet must read as a two-player cabinet; a repeat of empty panel does not satisfy the resize rule.
In the solid three-quarters view the door button boxes sit offset from the coin door face, floating beside/overlapping the door rather than seated on it in a tidy 2x2 group.
Door remains static with motion set to none instead of hinging open.
Lower cabinet door does not open when moving parts are actuated.
Widened version fragments control deck artwork rather than producing a clean two-player layout.

wider_means: A wider arcade cabinet is a two-player cabinet, with a second joystick, button set and start button on the control deck.
taller_means: A taller arcade cabinet is a taller cabinet body: more plain panel below the control deck and a longer lower door and kick area, not a taller screen or marquee.

faults.fault: At 2x width (image 3) the control deck simply extends as blank panel across the new width -- no second joystick, button cluster or start button appears. A wider cabinet must read as a two-player deck; more empty surface where the controls should be is a blocking sense fault, not just a texture issue.

At 1.5x height (image 4) the front panel stretches vertically: the marquee art, screen surround and door panels are smeared/streaked and the screen opening itself is dragged upward, instead of the extra height appearing as plain panel below the control deck and a longer kick area. The background is being stretched, not extended.
The stretched vertical tiling shows banding/streaking in the lower panels of image 4 -- texture smear visible where the prop was enlarged.
In image 4 the marquee area is carried up with the stretched body, so the marquee floats with a stretched void around it rather than staying a fixed cap on a taller cabinet.
Widened cabinet does not duplicate controls for a second player.
Door hinge and vertical scaling cause geometry to obscure the monitor when extended.
Width scaling distorts the coin door fixture instead of maintaining proper center framing.

faults.fault: At 2.0x width the deck stretches into blank, banded striping with no second joystick, button cluster or start button appearing -- a wider two-player cabinet is not represented; the repeated middle reads as smeared texture, not duplicated controls (image 3).

When the cabinet is made 1.5x taller the background panel stretches into a large smeared, streaked blank slab that climbs up over the control deck and screen area, hiding the front elevation layout (image 4).
In the taller render the coin-door/kick region is distorted: the lower door area is cut and doubled, and the marquee/decal rows no longer read as one object (image 4).

With the door driven open (image 5) the door slab juts past the body silhouette and collides with the control-deck overhang / lower-body corner instead of swinging cleanly out from its own face; in the wireframe the open door reads as a box intersecting the cabinet rather than hinged off it.
Redundant geometry duplicating the lower facade that detaches and floats during vertical resize.
Spans horizontally on wide resize instead of retaining standard fixed proportions.
Remains fixed width, failing to bridge the cabinet width when widened.

taller_means: A taller arcade cabinet is a taller cabinet body: more plain panel below the control deck and a longer lower door and kick area, not a taller screen or marquee.

faults.fault: At 2x width the deck plank stretches/repeats across the full width but no second joystick, button cluster or start button appears -- the deck repeats its blank texture instead of its controls, so the wider cabinet does not read as a two-player cabinet. Blocking.

Marquee art is anchored top and fixed, so when the cabinet widens the marquee shows tiled/doubled artwork (extra star field slabs with visible seams beside the title) instead of one continuous marquee. Blocking.

In the 1.5x taller render the body texture is smeared and streaked vertically (grey banding across the screen area and lower panel), and the screen bay reads as a blank grey smear. Blocking tiling/stretch fault.

In the three-quarter solid view a slab of the deck protrudes past the left side of the body and floats clear of it, reading as a loose plank rather than part of the cabinet. Blocking floating-geometry fault.
Upper service panel swings open and clips through the cabinet side wall; it should be static.
Vertical scaling stacks duplicate screen and upper cabinet geometry instead of extending the lower base.
Widening cabinet smears controls rather than configuring a valid two-player control layout.
Marquee texture splits and distorts when widened instead of cleanly extending framing.
